title: Reconciliation: a disagreement, a refused correction, and a posted entry
summary: The simulated scheme's own statement is generated and posted straight back for matching — first the true one, which matches every line and opens no break, then a deliberately wrong one, which opens a break with its kind and its detail. The break is assigned, a correction is proposed, its proposer is refused when he tries to approve it himself, a checker rejects it with a reason, a second correction is proposed and approved, and the journal entry that resolves the break is read back. Nothing edits an entry: the books move by a new fact about a new moment.
source: clofin-core docs/uat/UAT-007-reconciliation-and-breaks.md steps 1 to 12, driven through a browser. The statement posted for ingestion is the document the instance returned, with the organisation id added — the same thing UAT-007 does with jq.
unverifiable: That re-delivering a statement changes nothing in the database. The receipt says replayed: true and returns the same id, which is shown; the counts UAT-007 §3 checks are SQL.

That one posted adjustment per break is guaranteed. The guard is a partial unique index in the schema, so it binds a fix-up script as well as a handler — which is exactly why a browser cannot demonstrate it (UAT-007 §11).
That the original journal entries were untouched. This flow reads the new entry the adjustment posted; that the earlier ones are unchanged is a property of an append-only table, checked in SQL.
The break's age. ageSeconds is derived when the break is read and stored nowhere, so the figure shown is true at the moment of that response and not afterwards.

steps.title: Ask the simulated scheme for its statement
steps.why: The scheme's own account of what it did, computed from the settlement records. The format is CloFin's own — SIM-CLOFIN-RECON-STATEMENT — and is deliberately not camt.053, MT940, BAI2 or any real scheme's schema. Count the lines against the batch: a payment the scheme never answered about produces no line at all, and its value is still sitting in 1300-IN-TRANSIT where value of unknown fate belongs.

readouts.label: 1300-IN-TRANSIT, before any matching
readouts.why: Whatever is left here is what the scheme has not accounted for. Read from the instance so the number beside the statement is the ledger's own.

steps.title: Post that statement straight back, and watch it match
steps.why: The document below is the one the instance just returned, unchanged, with organisationId added — nothing was retyped, because retyping it would be this page asserting what the scheme said. Every line matches, each carrying the rule that made the match: R1-reference-amount-and-value-date. A match that could not say how it was made is a match nobody can defend. breaks is empty, and that is the correct answer for a statement that agrees.

subjects.label: The receipt for the unperturbed statement

steps.title: Ask for a statement that is wrong in a named way
steps.why: A generator that could only produce agreement could not test disagreement. amount-mismatch is one of six named classes, so you can predict the break before you run anything: same payment, different amount. The statementReference differs from the true one because the perturbation is part of it, which is what makes this a second document rather than a contradiction of the first.

steps.title: Ingest it, and open a break
steps.why: The break carries the kind the class predicts, a detail naming what disagreed rather than merely that something did, state open, an assigneeId — a break is never unowned, and opens assigned to whoever ingested the statement that found it — and an ageSeconds derived when it is read. All of that is the instance's; this page renders it.

subjects.label: The break the perturbed statement opened

steps.title: Sam assigns the break to Wei
steps.why: Assigning a break is how it becomes investigated: taking it on is one fact, not two. Re-assigning it later would change the owner and not the state, because re-assignment is not a transition.

readouts.label: The break, as it now stands
readouts.why: State, owner and age, read back from the instance rather than assumed from the response to the assignment.

steps.title: Sam proposes a correction — SGD 1,000.00
steps.why: At exactly SGD 1,000.00 the organisation's band applies, so this needs somebody else's agreement. proposed, posted false, and the break still investigating: a proposed adjustment resolves nothing.

body.narrative: Provisional: the scheme's figure looks wrong

subjects.label: The correction that will be refused

steps.title: Sam tries to approve his own correction — and is refused
steps.why: The same control that refused the maker approving her own payment: the same function, the same table, the same refusal vocabulary. There is no second approval mechanism in CloFin. The expected outcome of this step is 403 with errors.reason self-approval, and the prose names the subject — the actor who created this reconciliation adjustment may not approve it.

steps.title: Wei refuses it, with a reason
steps.why: Not every proposal deserves to post. A refusal whose reason is retained is the difference between a trail that explains a declined correction and one that merely records that somebody declined it — the same rule PR-013 sets for a rejected payment, enforced in the domain and again by a database constraint. The adjustment becomes rejected with no entryId and an empty permittedTransitions: it is terminal, because a refusal that could be taken back would not be a refusal. The break returns to nothing, because proposing never moved it.

body.reason: The statement is right; our posting is the one to investigate

readouts.label: 1300-IN-TRANSIT, after the refusal
readouts.why: Unchanged. A refused correction moves no money, and this is read from the instance rather than asserted.

readouts.label: The break, after the refusal
readouts.why: Still investigating. A refused correction blocks nothing and resolves nothing.

steps.title: Sam proposes a different correction against the same break
steps.why: A refused correction blocks nothing: the one-posted-adjustment-per-break index is partial on posted, so a rejected row sits outside it. This is the second proposal, on its own merits.

body.narrative: Agreed after investigation: parked in suspense pending the scheme's correction

steps.title: Wei agrees — one of the approvals this needs
steps.why: The organisation's band at SGD 1,000.00 asks for two. Read approvalsHeld and approvalsRequired in the response: they are the instance's count, and posted is still false. An approved-but-unposted adjustment is not a state that exists, so nothing has moved yet either.

steps.title: Nadia agrees — and the books move, in the same transaction
steps.why: posted true, the adjustment posted, and the break resolved, all at once. The entry it posted is an ordinary journal entry with two balancing lines, one on 1300-IN-TRANSIT and one on 2200-UNAPPLIED. Nothing was edited: the original entries are untouched and this is a new fact about a new moment.

subjects.label: The entry that resolved the break

readouts.label: 1300-IN-TRANSIT, after the correction posted
readouts.why: Moved by the adjustment, and read from the instance. The figure is minor units exactly as reported.

readouts.label: 2200-UNAPPLIED, after the correction posted
readouts.why: The other side of the same entry. The account where a difference sits while somebody finds out what it was.

readouts.label: The break, now
readouts.why: resolved, in the same transaction that posted the entry.

steps.title: Read the entry the correction posted
steps.why: Two lines, balancing, referencing reconciliation-adjustment. This is what it means for the books to move here: not an edit, but an entry — the same doctrine a correction to a settled payment follows, where the fix is a reversing instruction rather than a change of mind about an old one.

subjects.label: The entry that resolved the break

readouts.label: The entry's own reference and lines
readouts.why: Projected out of the response beside it. Directions and amounts are the instance's; nothing here is summed.
